findings.claim: Measuring Wave Speed — Practical Activity (PAG P4 & P11) ... For investigating wave speed in a stretched string (PAG P11)
findings.truth: J249 has eight Practical Activity Groups, P1 to P8 (P1 Materials, P2 Forces, P3 Motion, P4 Measuring waves, P5 Energy, P6 Circuit components, P7 Series and parallel circuits, P8 Interactions of waves). There is no PAG P11, and no stretched-string practical is listed. The ripple-tank work is PAG P4.
findings.evidence: spec Topic P9 PAG table (physics-a-gateway-J249.md lines 5420-5520): groups P1-P8 only

findings.claim: higher-only wrapper around n29 (speed of sound depends on stiffness and density; faster in solids than liquids than gases)
findings.truth: P5.1f is a separate-science statement (þ) but is NOT bold, so it is assessed at both Foundation and Higher Tier. The wrapper hides both-tier content from Foundation students; it has been used to mean 'separate-only'.
findings.evidence: bold spec P5.1f 'show how changes, in velocity, frequency and wavelength, in transmission of sound waves from one medium to another, are inter-related' — plain text, not **bold**

findings.claim: A whole section teaches diffraction (n21, n24, key fact n25), plus a 3-mark practice question, a fill knowledge check, an exam-tip sentence and three flashcards.
findings.truth: The word 'diffraction' does not appear anywhere in J249 (grep of the full spec returns zero hits). Reflection (P5.1g) and refraction (P5.3c/d) are in scope; diffraction is not. Coordinator ruling: label only — no deletion, and the practice question and knowledge check stay for now. An unnarrated scope-note paragraph is inserted straight after the heading that opens the diffraction material, telling students the topic is background and that exam questions will ask about reflection and refraction instead. No div change and no narration id.
findings.evidence: grep -i 'diffract' specs/ocr/physics-a-gateway-J249.md → 0 hits

findings.claim: higher-only paragraph n24: 'The power of a lens is defined as P = 1/f ... measured in dioptres (D) ... a +2 D lens has a focal length of 0.5 m'
findings.truth: Lens power and dioptres are not on J249 at any tier. P5.3c and P5.3d restrict lenses to ray diagrams, 'qualitative only – equations not needed'. Labelling off-spec content 'Higher tier' tells a student it is examined when it is not. In the same sub-topic, P5.3e (colour from differential absorption, transmission and reflection, with specular reflection and scattering) is a separate-science both-tier statement that this unit teaches nowhere. The edit replaces the dioptre paragraph with P5.3e content and drops the wrapper; the narration block is kept, so the block count is unchanged.
findings.evidence: bold spec P5.3c/P5.3d '(qualitative only – equations not needed)'; P5.3e present and not bold; grep 'dioptre' in spec → 0 hits

findings.claim: 'Unstable nuclei emit three main types of ionising radiation:' — neutron emission is never mentioned in the lesson.
findings.truth: P6.1d and P6.1e both name neutrons alongside alpha, beta and gamma as emissions from unstable nuclei. A student asked to name what an unstable nucleus can emit could lose the neutron mark.
findings.evidence: bold spec P6.1d 'may emit alpha particles, beta particles, or neutrons, and electromagnetic radiation as gamma rays'; P6.1e likewise

findings.claim: Key takeaway n32: 'After \(n\) half-lives, \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^n\) of the original nuclei remain.'
findings.truth: The ratio calculation after an integral number of half-lives is P6.1k, which is bold and therefore Higher Tier only. The lesson body correctly hides it behind a higher-only wrapper (n22), but the conclusion repeats it to every student unflagged. Half-life itself (P6.1j) stays both-tier.
findings.evidence: bold spec **P6.1k** 'calculate the net decline, expressed as a ratio, during radioactive emission after a given (integral) number of half-lives'

findings.claim: Description is 111 characters.
findings.truth: The house validator caps lesson descriptions under 100 characters. At 111 the record would be rejected when the other edits are written back.
findings.evidence: measured length of the description string

findings.claim: 'Contamination (radioactive material on/in the body) is more dangerous than irradiation (external exposure)'
findings.truth: Stated as an absolute. It is true for an ingested alpha emitter but not universally — a large external gamma dose can be worse. The body text says 'generally considered more dangerous', which is right; the takeaway drops the hedge. Not worth an edit on its own.
findings.evidence: spec P6.2a asks learners to 'compare the hazards associated with these two', not to rank them absolutely

findings.claim: Description is 102 characters.
findings.truth: Over the house validator's 100-character cap for lesson descriptions.

findings.claim: higher-only wrapper around n31 (lubrication, streamlining, thermal insulation, LED lighting)
findings.truth: P7.2f 'explain ways of reducing unwanted energy transfer', to include lubrication and thermal insulation, is not bold and so is assessed at both tiers. Only P7.2e 'describe ways to increase efficiency' is bold. The wrapper also contradicts this lesson's own conclusion (n39) and flashcard 12, which state the same content unflagged.

findings.claim: higher-only wrapper around the whole 'Elastic Potential Energy and Hooke's Law' collapsible (n32-n34)
findings.truth: PM2.3ii (energy transferred in stretching = ½ × spring constant × extension²) is a select-and-apply equation and is not bold; P7.1e requires learners to 'calculate the amounts of energy associated with a moving body, a stretched spring and an object raised above ground level'. Both are assessed at both tiers, so the wrapper hides required Foundation content.

findings.claim: 'a motor receives 500 J of electrical energy and transfers 350 J as useful kinetic energy, its efficiency = 350/500 = 0.70, or 70%. The remaining 130 J is wasted'
findings.truth: 500 − 350 = 150 J, not 130 J. Lesson 6 uses the identical example and correctly says 150 J.
findings.evidence: recomputation: 500 − 350 = 150

findings.claim: Carbon dioxide written as CO<sup>2</sup> in five places
findings.truth: The formula is CO<sub>2</sub>. A superscript 2 renders as CO², which is not a chemical formula and would not be credited if copied.
findings.evidence: settled chemical formula

findings.claim: higher-only wrapper around n27 (lubrication, insulation, streamlining, better materials)
findings.truth: Same fault as F10: P7.2f is both-tier. Worse here, because the lesson's own 6-mark extended-response question asks 'Describe two ways in which energy losses in a device can be reduced', and the conclusion (n35) states the same content unflagged, so a Foundation student is examined on material the page hides from them.
findings.evidence: bold spec P7.2f plain text

findings.claim: higher-only wrapper around n29 and n30 (National Grid, P = I²R, step-up and step-down transformers)
findings.truth: P8.2c (high-voltage transmission, lower voltage locally), P8.2d (step-up and step-down transformers) and P8.2e (why the grid is efficient) are all plain, both-tier statements, and PM3.2iii (power = current² × resistance) is a recall-and-apply equation for both tiers. The wrapper is also contradicted by this lesson's unflagged 3-mark practice question and knowledge check on the same content, and by the Paper 1 unit, which teaches the grid unwrapped.

findings.claim: Match check [4]: right options are ['Braking distance only', 'Thinking distance only', 'Braking distance only'] — two identical options for three items.
findings.truth: A match item with two identical right-hand options cannot be marked reliably: a student pairing 'Worn tyres' with the third option gives the same answer in words but is marked wrong. Replacing the third pair with 'Higher speed' → 'Both thinking and braking distance' makes all three options distinct and tests the misconception the spec names for P8.1.
findings.evidence: answer-key inspection; bold spec P8.1 common misconceptions note on thinking versus braking distance

findings.claim: Momentum, p = mv, worked examples and conservation of momentum (n7-n23) are taught unflagged in a lesson tiered 'both', with matching untagged practice questions, knowledge checks and flashcards.
findings.truth: On J249 momentum is Higher Tier only: PM2.2ii (momentum = mass × velocity) and P2.2k (define momentum and describe examples of momentum in collisions, including conservation) are both bold. Foundation students are being taught and tested on content that cannot appear on their paper.
findings.evidence: bold spec **PM2.2ii** and **P2.2k**

findings.claim: n27: 'At Higher Tier, this is formalised using the equation \(F = \frac{\Delta p}{\Delta t}\)'
findings.truth: F = Δp/Δt is not on J249 at all. It appears in neither the recall-and-apply list nor the select-and-apply list, and 'rate of change of momentum' and 'impulse' return no hits in the spec. Telling students it is the Higher Tier formalisation is a false exam claim. The reasoning (longer collision time, smaller force) is right and stays.
findings.evidence: spec section 5d equations lists; grep 'rate of change of momentum|impulse' → 0 hits

findings.claim: Crumple-zone mark scheme cites '(F = Δp/Δt)'
findings.truth: Same off-spec equation as F18. The mark scheme reads correctly without it.

findings.truth: P8.3b 'explain how red shift and other evidence can be linked to the Big-Bang model', to include CMBR, is a separate-science statement but is not bold, so it is assessed at both tiers. findings.claim: 'The OCR specification uses a Doppler ball demonstration to model red-shift'
findings.truth: The spec lists the Doppler ball in the optional 'Practical suggestions' column for P8.3a; it does not require or 'use' it. The physics that follows (higher pitch approaching, lower pitch receding) is correct.
findings.evidence: bold spec P8.3a practical suggestions column 'Use of a Doppler ball to model red-shift'

findings.claim: Lesson-to-paper mapping and overlap with the Paper 1 unit.
findings.truth: The mapping of L1-L9 onto P5, P6, P7 and P8 is correct for Paper 2 (F2 / H4), and P8.3 space physics is rightly present as separate-only content. Two blocks are duplicated, though. L8 (stopping distances and momentum, P8.1 / P2.2) repeats separate-sciences-ocr/physics-paper-1 L4, and the National Grid collapsible in L7 (P8.2) repeats physics-paper-1 L7, which also carries UK mains 230 V / 50 Hz. On this spec P8 belongs to Paper 2, so the Paper 2 placement is the correct one and the Paper 1 copies are the strays. Recommend leaving both here, adding a one-line scope note in the Paper 1 unit, and deciding whether the Paper 1 copies keep their duplicate practice items.
findings.evidence: spec section 2a: 'Paper 2 assesses content from Topics P5-P8, with assumed knowledge of Topics P1-P4 and P9'

findings.claim: P5-P8 statements taught nowhere in this unit.
findings.truth: Gaps found, all separate-science content: P5.1g examples (ultrasound and sonar) are absent; P5.1h and P5.1i (sound to vibrations in solids, the ear, why hearing works over a limited frequency range) are absent — both Higher; P5.3e colour, specular reflection and scattering is absent — both tiers, addressed by F4 if that edit is accepted; P8.2g/h/i/j (UK mains 230 V 50 Hz, a.c. versus d.c., live, neutral and earth wires, live-wire dangers) sit in the Paper 1 unit instead; P8.3d (all bodies emit radiation, intensity and wavelength depend on temperature) is absent — both tiers; P8.3h (Earth's temperature balance) and P8.3i (P and S waves, sonar) are absent — both Higher. Recommend one added lesson covering P5.1g-i plus P8.3d and P8.3i, and moving the P8.2 mains statements into this unit alongside the grid.
findings.evidence: keyword sweep of raw/L01-L09 against the bold spec P5-P8 statement list

summary: One arithmetic error (L7: 500 − 350 given as 130 J) and one unmarkable match item (L8: two identical options). The dominant fault is tier wrappers used in both directions: four higher-only wrappers hide both-tier content (L1 speed of sound, L6 lubrication and elastic PE, L7 lubrication and the National Grid), while momentum in L8 is bold Higher-only content taught unflagged. Two off-spec claims: lens dioptres in L3 and F = Δp/Δt in L8, both presented as Higher Tier when neither is on J249; diffraction in L1 is also absent from the spec. Board anchors verified: four papers, 90 marks, 1 h 45 min, 50% each; PAGs P1-P8 (L1 cited a non-existent PAG P11); g = 10 N/kg. Every worked example, answer key and half-life table recomputed clean apart from the L7 case.
